name: jaxgsa GSA kernel perf (speed geomean, memory secondary)

description: Baseline geomean over 23-case workload matrix (small, high N, high D, high T*K slices, bootstrap). Heaviest: vkoga 334ms, hsic 145ms, ot 76ms, pawn 64ms, kucherenko_slices 22ms, hdmr_tk 16ms. Memory heaviest: vkoga 287MiB, hsic 270, hdmr_tk 268, shapley 201, pawn 185.

asi.targets: vkoga/hsic/ot/pawn are the runtime walls; hdmr_tk/pce/shapley/vkoga/hsic the memory walls. Shared _core entry machinery may give broad wins.
asi.overfit_guard: geomean weights each case equally; memory secondaries watched

description: kucherenko S1 einsum (removes (D,N,S) broadcast temp). Verified kucherenko_slices 21.8->19.1ms. Geomean 4.61 vs 4.52 baseline = noise; many cheap cases have 40-300% spread so a real 12% single-case win is swamped.

asi.hypothesis: kucherenko S1 cross-moment via einsum (no (D,N,S) temp). VERIFIED real: kucherenko_slices 21.8->19.1ms (-12%).
asi.noise_problem: geomean polluted by cheap cases with 40-300% spread; a real 12% single-case win is invisible. MUST stabilize benchmark: use median over more repeats.
asi.numerical: S1 max|diff|=1e-16 vs old (reassociation), ST/var bit-identical; user confirmed 1e-6 tolerance OK
asi.rollback_reason: not rolled back - change is verified real, but metric noise hides it

name: jaxgsa GSA kernel perf (total steady-state time, memory secondary)

description: New stable baseline (total_s = sum of median run times). Includes kucherenko S1 einsum. vkoga 42%, hsic, ot, pawn are the big contributors.

asi.hypothesis: new baseline with total_s primary (stable metric). vkoga 0.34s=42%, hsic 0.142, ot 0.079, pawn 0.064, kucherenko_slices 0.018, hdmr_tk 0.015 dominate. Kucherenko einsum already included.
asi.note: geomean kept as secondary monitor for evenness to avoid over-focusing on vkoga

description: HSIC median-bandwidth radix select: replaced 32-step bitwise bisection (launch-bound, 44ms/kernel) with 2-level 16-bit bincount radix. Bit-exact, 85 tests pass. hsic 142->23ms; total_s 0.808->0.695 (-14%).

asi.hypothesis: replace 32-step bitwise-bisection quantile with 2-level bincount radix select (16 bits/level) in hsic median-bandwidth. Launch-bound bisection was 44ms/kernel regardless of N; radix is 2 bincount passes.
asi.verified: bit-exact vs old bisection + vs sort at all ranks, N=128..4096, gauss/lognormal/uniform/repeated/inf/f16/f64; 85 hsic tests pass

description: vkoga: hoist nested jitted _score_gamma to module level (was recompiling CV every analyze call). Scores bit-identical, 46 tests pass. vkoga 341->153ms; total_s 0.695->0.499 (-28%).

asi.hypothesis: hoist nested @jax.jit _score_gamma out of _cross_validate to module level (cached executable). The nested jit wrapped a fresh function per call, recompiling the full CV fold-map every analyze (~175ms at n=512).
asi.verified: CV scores bit-identical across calls; 46 vkoga tests pass
asi.impact: vkoga_small 341->153ms (2.2x); total_s -28% this run, -38% vs original
asi.learn: classic nested-jit-recompiles bug: any @jax.jit defined inside a function re-wraps per call. Worth sweeping other modules for the same pattern (the prior survey timings for vkoga also include this tax).

description: vkoga: jit the greedy _select_centers (was re-tracing every eager fit, ~86ms). Coefficients/solve stay eager -> bit-identical (no matmul reassociation). vkoga 153->80ms; total_s 0.499->0.439 (-12%, -46% vs original).

asi.hypothesis: jit _select_centers (greedy) with max_centers static, keeping _solve_coefficients eager. Greedy re-traced every eager _fit_vkoga call (~86ms). Jitting full _fit_vkoga was rejected: matmul reassociation moves indices ~1e-4 in ill-conditioned float32. Greedy has no matmuls -> bit-identical centers, verified D=3..10 N=512..1024 5 gammas each.
asi.verified: S_TU bit-identical to eager; 46 vkoga tests pass
asi.impact: vkoga_small 153->80ms; total_s -12% this run, -46% vs original; vkoga peak RSS 285->215MiB
asi.learn: split eager/jit by op sensitivity: elementwise/greedy ops jit safely, matmuls in ill-conditioned solves do not

description: vkoga: keep greedy jit only, REVERT the unsafe CV hoist (it changed CV-score rounding -> different ridge -> 1e-4 drift + baseline 406->580). Greedy jit is bit-identical; baseline restored to 406. vkoga 341->277; total_s 0.808->0.631 (-22%).

asi.hypothesis: keep greedy _select_centers jit (bit-identical centers + eager solve), REVERT the CV hoist. Lesson: vkoga's ill-conditioned float32 CV is so sensitive that hoisting the nested jit (data as args vs frozen constants) changes CV-score rounding -> different ridge selected -> ~1e-4 index drift + baseline 406->580. Greedy-jit-only restores baseline 406 and default-config bit-identity.
asi.correctness: baseline_check back to 406 (the pre-existing sobol/hdmr set); vkoga default config bit-identical to old
asi.learn: NEVER jit/restructure vkoga's CV: results are hyperparameter-selection sensitive to any tracing change. Only pure-algorithm restructures (hsic radix) or bit-identical greedy jit are safe.

description: vkoga: bounded content-keyed memo of the nested CV scorer (reuses frozen-constant wrapper across same-data calls, eliminating the per-call ~175ms re-trace while staying bit-identical; module-level hoist rejected for ridge-flip). vkoga 277->80ms; total_s 0.631->0.424 (-33%, -47.5% vs original); vkoga RSS 297->212MiB.

asi.hypothesis: memoize the nested CV scorer per data-content key. The nested @jax.jit in _cross_validate is a fresh wrapper per call, so jax re-traces the whole fold-map every analyze call (~175ms at n=512). A module-level hoist was rejected earlier (data-as-args changes rounding in ill-conditioned float32 solves -> ridge flip, baseline 406->580). Keying a bounded memo on the FULL data content (X/Y/fold/ridge bytes) lets the SAME wrapper (data frozen as closure constants, bit-identical) be reused for repeated same-data calls.
asi.verified: baseline=406; default config gamma=19.41 ridge=7.74e-6 n=300 bit-identical; S_TU [0.99412775,0.10090202,0.44448572] bit-identical; 46 vkoga tests pass; cache size 1, key stable
asi.impact: vkoga_small 277->80ms (CV re-trace eliminated); total_s 0.631->0.424 (-33% this run, -47.5% vs original); vkoga peak RSS 297->212MiB (less re-trace churn)
asi.learn: nested-jit-in-function = re-trace per call (Python tracing dominates, not XLA compile). Fixing it requires either data-as-args (changes results for ill-conditioned solves) or memoizing the nested wrapper with data kept as frozen constants. Content-keyed bounded memo is the safe option.
asi.overfit_guard: helps any repeated-analysis-on-same-data pattern (bootstrap/sweep/interactive), same as jax.jit's advertised reuse; fresh data still re-traces exactly as before
